html:
The Baqt was a treaty agreed in 652 between the Christian Nubian kingdom of Makuria and the Muslim Arab rulers of Egypt. By some measures it is the longest-lasting treaty in history.

After taking Egypt in the Arab conquests, an army under Abdallah ibn Sa'd marched up the Nile and besieged the Makurian capital, Dongola. Nubian archers held them off, and the Arabs agreed to terms instead of conquest. Makuria kept its independence and its religion. Each year it sent 360 enslaved people south to north; Egypt sent back wheat, cloth and wine. Each side let the other's traders pass in safety.

The deal held, with breaks, for about six hundred years. It let Christian Nubia flourish, building churches like the cathedral of Faras with its murals. It broke down in the late 13th century when the Mamluk sultans of Egypt began to meddle in Makurian affairs and set their own candidates on the throne.
sum: The Baqt was a treaty agreed in 652 between the Christian Nubian kingdom of Makuria and the Muslim Arab rulers of Egypt. By some measures it is the longest-lasting treaty in history.
